subject: Civil Engineering
title: Slump Test: Measuring Workability
description: A quick, practical guide to Slump Test: Measuring Workability.

hook.text: Fill a metal cone with concrete, lift it, and measure how much the pile slumps. That's the test.

buildup.text: A 4-inch slump is stiff — good for pavements. An 8-inch slump flows — good for pumping.

discovery.text: Slump correlates with water content. Too much slump means too much water — weaker concrete.

twist.text: Self-consolidating concrete has infinite slump — it flows like syrup without vibration.

climax.text: Every truckload of concrete is slump-tested before pouring — the simplest quality check.

punchline.text: A metal cone and a ruler control the quality of billions of tons of concrete.

quiz.question: What does a higher-than-specified slump typically indicate?
options: The concrete has too much aggregate
Too much water was added, which weakens the concrete
The cement has expired and lost its bonding ability
